doc: Observation vocabulary per flow. The client re-observes and re-reports EVERY predicate on EVERY 'what's next' call — nothing is remembered client-side, and the service never asks for a value. Booleans only. `ownership` says who the fact belongs to: a local-fact is observed by the CLI (the CLI owns the answer — it is never a filesystem probe by another process) and may steer SEQUENCING only, never authorization; a server-fact is owned by the service and is authoritative even when the client can see something that looks like it.

repo_fingerprint.definition: sha256 hex of the CLI's attached repository identity, reported at most once per flow instance (the FIRST value reported is what the instance records). Optional per report: a client that has not yet resolved a local repository identity omits it.
repo_fingerprint.why: Chunk 1 (docs/onboarding/level-set-2026-09-03.md, Codex 2026-09-03 cross-repository guard): "one open flow per user" must never silently attach another repository's request to an existing flow. The FIRST reported fingerprint is recorded on the flow instance (routes/flows.ts POST /:id/next, store.ts flows.repo_fingerprint); a later report naming a DIFFERENT one is refused with 409 FLOW_OPEN_FOR_OTHER_REPO and the flow is left unchanged.

report_schema.doc: The body of POST /flows/:id/next for an onboard instance (chunk 1). This is NOT the full local-fact predicate set the demolished onboard flow type once carried: chunk 1 implements exactly one server-driven trigger (signup readiness, advanced by the service's own push/pull derivation, never by a client report) and one cross-repository guard. `observations` therefore carries at most one optional field.

code.description: Closed set for onboard's chunk-1 report envelope, same shape as checkout's own last_step (checkoutEngine.ts). No local_action verb has a live executor yet (pair_runtime is chunk 2), so this stays the generic subset shared with checkout's own codes rather than minting codes for triggers that do not exist yet.

repoMatchesProject.definition: The attached directory's keep.lock names the project this flow instance was minted for (the plan's pinned project_id).
repoMatchesProject.why: BASE. checkout is minted server-side against a named project/branch (POST /flows/checkout resolves both at creation), but the CLI reporting observations may be running in ANY directory — this is the check that the directory it is actually sitting in is the one the plan is about, before it ever attempts a local branch switch. A mismatch is never silently proceeded through: see blocked_reasons.wrong_repo.
repoMatchesProject.source: the checkout flow's own plan (checkoutEngine.ts); the CLI's local keep.lock read, the same file hasKeepLock/orgKeyOnDevice already read for onboard

switchCompleted.definition: The CLI's local `switch_branch` executor has already put the working copy on the plan's pinned branch, for the plan this flow instance holds.
switchCompleted.why: BASE. The single fact this flow exists to prove: once true, the flow is done. Gates the one local_action verb this flow ever issues (switch_branch), the same convergence guarantee every onboard verb's flip predicate gives — a level-triggered re-ask converges once the switch has actually happened.
switchCompleted.source: the CLI's checkout flow executor (capy-cli) — see steps.json local_action_verbs.switch_branch

report_schema.doc: The body of POST /flows/:id/next for a checkout instance. The client re-observes and re-reports EVERY predicate on every call; nothing is remembered client-side, same discipline as onboard.

code.description: Closed set for checkout's own report envelope. BRANCH_SWITCH_FAILED is minted for this flow (steps.json blocked_reasons.branch_switch_failed); NETWORK_ERROR/SERVICE_ERROR are the same existing codes onboard's own report schema already carries, reused rather than re-minted.
